checks: Matched f17e4f2b0ba9ee84 §2, (1)–(3), against the source digest. The frozen statement preserves nonnegative upper semicontinuity, so weights may vanish on the boundary, and proves precisely the local logarithmic ingredients rather than the later compactness claim.

Upper semicontinuity on compact K gives a maximizer v and positivity on its full-dimensional interior gives m>0. The set (1−t)K+tv is contained in the superlevel {L≥tm} and has volume (1−t)^d|K|, also at both endpoints in d≥1.

The event −log(L/m)>s is precisely {L<e^(−s)m}; the complement uses the stated closed superlevel. Its probability is at most 1−(1−e^(−s))^d. Integration gives the finite harmonic sum by the identity [1−(1−t)^d]/t=∑_{j=0}^{d−1}(1−t)^j. This proves absolute integrability of log L, even when L=0 at boundary points. The opposite bound is pointwise L≤m.

The same superlevel estimate integrated from zero to one yields mean L≥m/(d+1). The centroid is interior and a finite concave function admits a supergradient there. That bound extends to every point of K by the concavity inequality along its segment from the centroid and therefore integrates to Jensen's inequality without requiring boundary continuity.

An actual compatible anchored combination of maximizing points lies in the target fiber, so joint concavity gives the sampled maximum inequality. Summing the two logarithmic inequalities with original weights V_z/M and using zero mixed log mean gives 0≤∑w_z log m_z≤H_d.

Checked exact boundary calibrations: a barycentric coordinate on the standard simplex has superlevel volume ratio (1−t)^d, log mean −H_d and centroid value 1/(d+1). The upper log bound is attained by a constant. Recomputed the harmonic integral and mean from their binomial expansions in dimensions 1 through 30.

It does not supply the harmonic logarithmic integral bound or mixed log-normalized maximum bounds in the nonnegative upper-semicontinuous class.

Controls logarithmic integrals of concave weights through assumed contact certificates and a variational inequality. The present single-weight logarithmic estimate needs no contact certificate and derives from level-volume scaling.

Concerns a finite atomic inverse-power escort optimization at a prescribed base mean. The logarithm here is integrated against the actual Lebesgue-volume law of each fiber, with no escort or inverse-power optimization.

readability: The logarithm may be assigned −infinity at zeros. Such points are confined to the volume-null boundary, and the proved tail estimate handles integrability directly.
